prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2025-10-30. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 0.79 |
| Retained earnings       | 8,995M |
| Current liabilities     | 7,148M |
| Current assets          | 5,681M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 21,181M |
| Total liabilities       | 57,973M |
| Total assets            | 79,154M |
| EBIT / operating income | 749M |
| Revenue                 | 3,915M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2025-10-30, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company exhibits a very low current ratio (0.79), indicating short-term liquidity challenges and difficulty covering immediate obligations. The substantial total liabilities (57,973M) compared to total assets (79,154M) and shareholders' equity (21,181M) suggests a high leverage, further exacerbated by a relatively low EBIT margin (749M/3,915M = 19.1%) which might not be sufficient to service such a large debt burden. These factors point towards a significant risk of default without substantial improvements in operational performance or financial restructuring.

DECISION: B-
